title: DSCR Investor Loan: Qualify With $0 Tax Returns

title: Section 1031 Exchange: Sell Real Estate & Pay $0 Capital Gains
full_script: If you sell an investment property, the IRS could take up to 40% of your profits in capital gains and depreciation recapture. On a 500,000 dollar gain, federal capital gains, state taxes, and 25% depreciation recapture can eat 160,000 dollars of your hard-earned equity. Under IRS Section 1031, you can legally defer 100% of the tax by rolling your full net proceeds into a like-kind replacement property. You have 45 days to identify and 180 days to close. You keep 100% of your equity compounding into larger, cash-flowing commercial assets instead of handing it to the government. title: Bank Statement Mortgage: Buy a Home Without Tax Returns
full_script: If you're a business owner or 1099 freelancer, your tax write-offs are probably disqualifying you from buying a house. Traditional mortgage underwriters look at line 31 of your Schedule C. If you write off expenses to lower taxes, your qualifying income shows as zero. With a 12-Month Bank Statement mortgage, lenders calculate qualifying income directly from your business deposits. They total 12 months of gross deposits, apply an industry expense ratio like 50%, and divide by 12. A business owner depositing 40,000 dollars a month qualifies for a 1,200,000 dollar mortgage, even with zero net tax return income. title: Structured Settlement Lump Sum: Don't Let Factoring Firms Rob You
full_script: If you have a structured settlement or legal annuity, factoring companies are trying to take 60% of your money. Commercial TV commercials offer fast cash for settlements, but they slip in predatory discount rates between 14% and 22%. Under IRC Section 5891, your payout must be discounted to net present value. 250,000 dollars paid over 10 years at a fair 9% rate is worth 157,000 dollars. At an 18% rate, they only give you 98,000 dollars. That is a 59,000 dollar rip-off. Know your actuarial fair market value before talking to factoring brokers so you can negotiate a competitive discount rate under 9%. title: Cap Rate & Debt Yield: How Commercial Banks Value Buildings
full_script: Want to know how commercial banks and syndicators price 10-million-dollar apartment buildings? Beginners only look at Cap Rate. But institutional lenders don't care about cap rate; they size loans using Debt Yield and DSCR. Cap Rate equals Net Operating Income divided by Purchase Price. But lenders require a minimum 9.5% to 10% Debt Yield, calculated as NOI divided by Loan Amount. Even if your Cap Rate is 6%, a low debt yield will slash your loan proceeds by hundreds of thousands of dollars. Accurately forecast loan proceeds, cash-on-cash yield, and valuation before signing a purchase agreement. Run institutional CRE underwriting calculations for free at omnioperand.com.
